terms.explain: Scientists label heights in the air by pressure. Lower pressure means higher up. We convert pressure to kilometres; the conversion is approximate.
How fast something is changing. A change of one kelvin is exactly a change of one degree Celsius.

terms.plain: Compared with normal for that month
terms.explain: July is always warmer than January. To see real change we compare each July only with other Julys, each January only with other Januarys.
The measurements move in one direction so steadily that random ups and downs are very unlikely to explain it.
We cannot tell the change apart from random ups and downs. It does not mean nothing changed. More years of data may settle it.

terms.plain: Very likely between X and Y
terms.explain: No measurement is exact. The range shows where the true value very likely lies.
The lowest layer of air, from the ground up to roughly 12 km. Clouds, rain and storms happen here.
From roughly 12 km to 50 km. Very dry and stable. The ozone layer is here.

terms.plain: A weather model corrected by real measurements
terms.explain: A computer model of the atmosphere that is constantly pulled toward what satellites, balloons and stations measured. It covers more years, but it can jump when its measuring instruments change.

terms.science: zonal mean of a latitude band
terms.explain: We average all the way around the planet at one distance from the equator. East and west differences are averaged out.
